question: When I am on a Skilled Worker visa, do I have to pay the IHS alongside the visa fee? Is my healthcare then free? And are my family covered too?
knowledge:
Skilled Worker applicants on the ordinary route pay the Immigration Health Surcharge as part of the visa application, in addition to the application fee. The Health and Care Worker visa is exempt.

Holders of this visa can use NHS services on broadly the same basis as a UK resident. Some services are charged separately: dental treatment and prescriptions in England are not free.

Dependants on the visa have the same NHS entitlement as the main visa holder.

question: I want to use Claude Code to build a system that automatically submits job applications. Can Claude Code write all of the code? Do job sites allow automated applications? And if I submit applications for other people, do I need their consent?
knowledge:
Claude Code is an AI coding tool that can write, run and debug code across a project. It does not guarantee that the resulting system is reliable, and automated browser systems tend to break when the target websites change.

Many job sites prohibit bots and automated applications in their terms of use, and may suspend accounts found using them.

Submitting applications on someone else's behalf involves processing their personal data. Under UK data protection law this requires a lawful basis, such as the person's consent or a contract with them.

question: My bachelor's degree is from outside the UK. Can I apply directly for a master's in the UK? What IELTS score do I need? And is my undergraduate average of 70% enough?
knowledge: Most UK universities accept a bachelor's degree from a recognised overseas university for entry to taught master's programmes, provided it is assessed as equivalent to a UK bachelor's degree.
parts: Whether an overseas bachelor's degree qualifies for master's entry
The IELTS score required
Whether a 70% average is enough

question: My bachelor's degree is from outside the UK. Can I apply directly for a master's in the UK? What IELTS score do I need? And is my undergraduate average of 70% enough?
knowledge:
Most UK universities accept a bachelor's degree from a recognised overseas university for entry to taught master's programmes, provided it is assessed as equivalent to a UK bachelor's degree.

Most taught master's programmes require IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, usually with no component below 6.0. Some universities accept 6.0 overall with no component below 5.5, depending on the subject, and some subjects require 7.0.

Where a master's programme sets a minimum undergraduate grade, the figure varies by university, by the country where the degree was taken, and often by the ranking of the home institution. There is no single conversion to the UK grading scale.

question: I'm renting a flat in England. Does my landlord have to protect my deposit? Is there a limit on how big the deposit can be? And can they keep part of it for normal wear and tear when I move out?
knowledge: For most private tenancies in England, a landlord who takes a deposit must protect it in a government-approved deposit protection scheme within 30 days of receiving it.
parts: Whether the deposit must be protected
Whether there is a limit on the deposit amount
Whether deductions can be made for normal wear and tear

question: I'm renting a flat in England. Does my landlord have to protect my deposit? Is there a limit on how big the deposit can be? And can they keep part of it for normal wear and tear when I move out?
knowledge:
For most private tenancies in England, a landlord who takes a deposit must protect it in a government-approved deposit protection scheme within 30 days of receiving it.

For most private tenancies in England, the deposit is capped at five weeks' rent where the annual rent is less than 50,000 pounds.

A landlord cannot make deductions from the deposit for fair wear and tear. Deductions can be made for damage beyond that, unpaid rent, or other breaches of the tenancy agreement.

question: I bought headphones online three weeks ago and they've stopped working. Can I get a full refund? Could I have returned them even if they weren't faulty? And who pays the postage to send them back?
knowledge:
Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, a consumer who rejects faulty goods within 30 days of taking ownership is usually entitled to a full refund.

For most goods bought online, a consumer can cancel the order for any reason within 14 days, starting from the day after the goods arrive.

When goods are returned because they are faulty, the retailer should cover the reasonable cost of returning them.

question: I work five days a week in England. How many days of paid holiday am I entitled to? Can my employer count bank holidays as part of that? And will I be paid for holiday I haven't taken when I leave?
knowledge:
Almost all workers are legally entitled to 5.6 weeks of paid holiday a year. For someone working five days a week, this is 28 days.

Employers can choose to include bank holidays as part of the statutory paid holiday entitlement.

When a worker leaves a job, they are entitled to be paid for any statutory holiday they have accrued but not taken.

question: I've just moved to Great Britain with a driving licence from my home country, which is outside the EU. Can I drive here on it? For how long? And can I swap it for a British licence without taking a test?
knowledge:
A new resident of Great Britain can drive a car on a valid full licence issued in another country.

Someone who becomes resident can drive on a licence from outside the EU and EEA for up to 12 months from the date they became resident.

Licences from designated countries can be exchanged for a GB licence without a test. Licences from other countries cannot be exchanged, and the holder must pass the GB driving tests.

question: Can my employer monitor my work emails? Do they have to tell me if they do? And if I ask for a copy of the personal data they hold about me, how quickly must they respond?
knowledge:
Employers can monitor workers' emails if the monitoring has a lawful basis under data protection law and is necessary and proportionate.

Workers should normally be told about monitoring, what it involves and why it is done. Covert monitoring is only justified in exceptional circumstances.

An organisation must usually respond to a subject access request within one month of receiving it. In most cases it cannot charge a fee.
